author: opus 5.5
body: [opus 5.5] Left open: the page half is done, the provider half is not. Done in vibe-talk, in the commits 'vibe-talk: put a reply the stream sent without its thread into that thread, and out of Main', 'vibe-talk: tell adapter authors to push message.thread, and test that the page receives it' and 'vibe-talk: wait for a read the page gave up on before placing what the stream left unplaced'. Once the channel's reads go quiet, the page reads All (reason=place, as a delta where it can) for every message the stream left without a thread record that those reads did not place. Any later copy that names the thread (that read, a delta, a page of any view, a replayed, edited or second live copy) moves the message out of Main into its thread in every column, with its counts, cards and the picker, and the reader keeps their place (#280 scroll-stability). A placing read that fails is asked again when the next read ends. The placing read is never sent beside a read of the channel the page gave up on that the server may still be answering (remote-ops-audit W7). It goes once that read's late answer has landed or failed, so that answer is still used. A placing read given up on is kept the same way: its late answer places the message, and the poll of the view on screen waits for it. The README push contract now documents message.thread, and an ingest test pins that it reaches the page unchanged. What remains: the provider adapter that pushes this channel's live messages still sends every one without a thread record. A threaded reply is therefore drawn on Main until the placing read lands: about as long as one read normally, and up to a minute or two while the chat service is slow, longer when a read before it was given up on. The fix is in that adapter's push: send the thread record its own reads give the message, and keep it across edits. That change is prepared outside this repository. Close this once the adapter sends the record and a live threaded reply is seen arriving straight in its thread. Unverified here: the behaviour against the real provider. Everything above was shown by the page suite, not on a deployment.
